rule: The autonomous loop MUST NOT optimize a product-critical subsystem unless that subsystem has a contract here AND a runnable evaluator. Registering a metric name without an evaluator is prohibited: scripts/audit-metric-contracts.ts fails if runnableBenchmarkExists is true and runnableCommand is missing or not a real package script, and tests/metric-contracts.test.ts asserts the same.

optimizationTarget.rationale: The standard difficulty tier saturates experience and direction NDCG at 1.000 with worst-case 1.000, so it can detect neither improvement nor regression. The hard tier has headroom and is stable from 12 people.

humanValidityBoundary: Every synthetic and planted-truth benchmark here measures RECOVERY OF A KNOWN CONSTRUCT FROM SYNTHETICALLY RENDERED LANGUAGE. None of them establishes real-world human validity of mapping, fit, or recommendation quality. Rows whose humanGoldExists is false may be used for autonomous engineering signal only.

contracts.productQuestion: Did TaskDNA correctly understand what work the person likes and dislikes?
contracts.construct: Continuous interpretation of generator-exposed preference language on construct-valid bipolar dimensions.
contracts.groundTruth: Synthetic hidden preference vector, included wherever the generator exposed stance-resolved directional language
contracts.aggregation: within-subject mean over available eligible dimensions, then equal subject mean
knownFailureModes: extraction recall about 0.31 leaves predictions pinned near the neutral prior
prediction variance under 10% of truth variance
recognizedOutsideAvailableRate about 0.66
goodhartRisks: shrinkage toward the prior
constant-5 collapse
generator-exposure drift
stance-lexicon widening
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative preference-interpretation quality between decoders on the synthetic construct
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: Experience accuracy, mapper accuracy, job-ranking quality, recommendation quality, human validity, or overall TaskDNA accuracy
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Whether an extracted preference matches what the person means requires human labelling.
contracts.currentLimitation: Only 2 of 17 dimensions are MAE-eligible. Available-to-recognized recall is 0.31.

contracts.productQuestion: Did TaskDNA correctly identify work the person ACTUALLY PERFORMED?
contracts.construct: Classification of a career statement as performed work rather than preference or aspiration, and its attribution to a canonical work unit.
contracts.predictionOutput: evidence class per statement, plus a canonical Task/DWA mapping
contracts.groundTruth: Planted channel and planted canonical atom for every rendered statement
contracts.aggregation: per-class precision / recall / F1, then macro F1
knownFailureModes: 11.8% of statements classified UNKNOWN and contribute nothing
experience recall 0.667: reframed first-person statements are missed
goodhartRisks: widening the exposure pattern until everything is experience
which the contamination counters expose
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative evidence-class accuracy on synthetically rendered statements
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-validated extraction accuracy on real resumes
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Independent human annotation of real career text is required for a real-world claim.
contracts.currentLimitation: Measures evidence CLASS, not atom-level span extraction. The V3 ranking path is supplied declared kinds, so class errors do not currently propagate into ranking.

contracts.productQuestion: Did TaskDNA correctly understand what work the person wants to do NEXT?
contracts.construct: Classification of a statement as a forward-looking aspiration, distinct from performed work and from present preference.
contracts.predictionOutput: evidence class per statement plus canonical mapping
contracts.groundTruth: Planted aspiration channel and planted atom
knownFailureModes: aspiration recall 0.708; 28 aspirations read as present-tense likes
person_direction mapping abstains on 54% of statements at hard difficulty
goodhartRisks: treating any future-tense sentence as an aspiration
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative aspiration-class accuracy on rendered statements
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-validated aspiration understanding
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Stated direction may differ from revealed direction; only the person can resolve that.
contracts.currentLimitation: Aspiration is the weakest mapping stream: 0.083 exact Top-1 at hard difficulty.

contracts.productQuestion: Did TaskDNA correctly identify the person's actual qualifications and capabilities?
contracts.construct: Extraction of skills, education, credentials, and capabilities from free text, with negation handling.
contracts.predictionOutput: structured qualification list with kind and negation flag
contracts.groundTruth: Planted qualification set
knownFailureModes: FREE-TEXT QUALIFICATION EXTRACTION IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. Qualifications reach V3 as structured input.
goodhartRisks: not applicable while unimplemented
contracts.allowedInterpretation: none
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: any claim that qualification extraction is evaluated
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Regulated credential equivalence has a legal answer no model should invent.
contracts.currentLimitation: No free-text qualification extractor exists. The structured path is verified end to end (pnpm bench:subsystems, requirements block) but that is plumbing verification, not extraction accuracy.
contracts.exclusion: EXCLUDED FROM THE 8-HOUR LOOP. The loop may not claim progress on qualification extraction. Qualification FIT (row 13) is separately measurable and remains in scope.

contracts.productQuestion: Given a statement about work the person performed, does TaskDNA identify the right canonical work?
contracts.construct: Recovery of a known canonical O*NET Task from paraphrased first-person language.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked Task candidates plus a Task / DWA / abstain decision
contracts.groundTruth: Planted atom's Task id and DWA ids
contracts.aggregation: accuracy and recall over statements, plus technical slices
contracts.naiveBaseline: lexical top-1 (the current implementation IS the lexical baseline)
knownFailureModes: 0.194 exact Top-1 at hard difficulty against 0.870 on the job side: compressed first-person language is far harder
short text (<=12 words) drops to 0.322 Top-1 with 31% abstention
goodhartRisks: lowering the abstention threshold to raise coverage while accuracy falls, which the coverage-accuracy curve exposes
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative mapping recovery from synthetically paraphrased language
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-validated mapping accuracy on real career text
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Real mapping accuracy needs independent human text-to-Task annotation.
contracts.currentLimitation: The planted target is a single Task. Acceptable-alternative Tasks are approximated by DWA-level agreement rather than by an annotated alternative set.

contracts.productQuestion: Given a stated like or dislike, does TaskDNA identify the work being referred to?
contracts.construct: Recovery of a known canonical Task from paraphrased preference language.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked Task candidates plus a Task / DWA / abstain decision
contracts.groundTruth: Planted atom's Task id and DWA ids
knownFailureModes: 0.179 exact Top-1 at hard difficulty; gerund reframing loses the leading verb
goodhartRisks: same abstention-threshold gaming as row 5
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative mapping recovery on preference language
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-validated mapping accuracy
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Same as row 5.
contracts.currentLimitation: Evaluated separately from experience mapping, as required, but shares one mapper implementation.

contracts.productQuestion: Given a stated aspiration, does TaskDNA identify the desired work?
contracts.construct: Recovery of a known canonical Task from paraphrased aspiration language.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked Task candidates plus a Task / DWA / abstain decision
contracts.groundTruth: Planted atom's Task id and DWA ids
knownFailureModes: worst stream: 0.083 exact Top-1 and 0.542 abstention at hard difficulty
goodhartRisks: same abstention-threshold gaming as row 5
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative mapping recovery on aspiration language
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-validated mapping accuracy
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Same as row 5.
contracts.currentLimitation: Aspiration framings add the most surface distance from the canonical statement, so this stream is the hardest.

contracts.productQuestion: Did TaskDNA correctly understand what work the JOB actually contains?
contracts.construct: Segmentation of a raw job description into distinct responsibilities, separated from requirements.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted responsibility set
knownFailureModes: FREE-TEXT RESPONSIBILITY SEGMENTATION IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. Responsibilities reach V3 as a structured list.
goodhartRisks: not applicable while unimplemented
contracts.allowedInterpretation: none
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: any claim that responsibility extraction is evaluated
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: What a job is really about is validated by people who do it.
contracts.currentLimitation: No JD segmenter exists. The benchmark supplies a structured responsibility list, so job-side Task mapping (row 9) is measurable while segmentation is not.
contracts.exclusion: EXCLUDED FROM THE 8-HOUR LOOP. The loop may not claim progress on responsibility segmentation. This is the single largest known coverage gap in the job-side pipeline.

contracts.productQuestion: Does TaskDNA map a job responsibility to the right canonical work, without letting the title decide?
contracts.construct: Recovery of a known canonical Task from paraphrased job-posting language.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked Task candidates plus a Task / DWA / abstain decision
contracts.groundTruth: Planted atom's Task id and DWA ids
mandatoryGuardrails: title leakage: SAME_TITLE_DIFFERENT_WORK must earn no experience credit
knownFailureModes: dwaHierarchicalAccuracy 0.120: when the mapper falls back to DWA it usually picks the wrong DWA
job-side mapping never abstains, so a wrong commit is never withheld
goodhartRisks: raising Top-1 by never abstaining, which the abstention metrics expose
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative mapping recovery on job language
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-validated mapping accuracy
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Same as row 5.
contracts.currentLimitation: 0.870 exact Top-1 against 0.194 on the person side: the asymmetry is the clearest single research target in the pipeline.

contracts.productQuestion: Do genuinely relevant jobs enter the candidate pool before any reranking?
contracts.construct: Retrieval recall over a controlled job pool, including across title and industry boundaries.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted experience/preference/direction relevance labels
contracts.naiveBaseline: title-only retrieval (0.346 recall) and lexical-overlap retrieval
knownFailureModes: canonical-work retrieval recall falls to 0.670 at hard difficulty while lexical-overlap holds 0.911: the canonical path is LESS robust to compressed language than the lexical one
goodhartRisks: retrieving everything to guarantee recall, which the concentration and diversity metrics expose
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative retrieval recall over a controlled pool
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: recall over a live job market
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Relevance here is planted, not human-judged.
contracts.currentLimitation: Controlled pool of a few hundred jobs, not a live market. LIVE POSTING INGESTION, freshness, and closed-job detection are out of scope for this loop.

contracts.productQuestion: Given work the person actually performed, do jobs containing transferable work rank appropriately regardless of title?
contracts.construct: Graded ranking quality against planted performed-work coverage.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted experience coverage grade 0-3
contracts.aggregation: macro mean NDCG@K over people, plus worst case
knownFailureModes: saturates at standard difficulty and must be run at hard difficulty to be informative
goodhartRisks: title leakage inflating rank, which the SAME_TITLE_DIFFERENT_WORK counter exposes
near-miss confusion, which HARD_NEAR_MISS exposes
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative experience-ranking quality on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-judged job relevance
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Human relevance judgement of person-job pairs is required for a product claim.
contracts.currentLimitation: 0.937 NDCG at hard difficulty leaves limited but real headroom; worst person is 0.786.

contracts.productQuestion: Do jobs containing work the person likes rank above jobs containing work they dislike?
contracts.construct: Graded ranking quality against signed planted liked-minus-disliked coverage.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted preference grade 0-3
mandatoryGuardrails: unknown/no-evidence behaviour must remain null rather than 0
knownFailureModes: a job with equal liked and disliked work scores exactly the neutral 0.5, indistinguishable from a job with no preference evidence (MIXED_PREFERENCE archetype)
goodhartRisks: scoring every job at the neutral centre to avoid dislike penalties, which variance and intrusion metrics expose
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative preference-ranking quality on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: predicted job satisfaction
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Whether a preference score predicts real satisfaction requires longitudinal human outcomes.
contracts.currentLimitation: 0.618 NDCG at hard difficulty: the weakest ranking channel and the largest ranking headroom.

contracts.productQuestion: Does TaskDNA correctly determine whether the person satisfies the job's requirements?
contracts.construct: Agreement between computed requirement satisfaction and planted qualification holdings.
contracts.predictionOutput: qualification channel score plus hard-gap diagnostics
contracts.groundTruth: Planted qualification set and planted required/preferred flags
contracts.aggregation: precision / recall over hard gaps, plus rank correlation with planted feasibility
mandatoryGuardrails: qualification must not alter any other channel score
knownFailureModes: ambiguous education and credential equivalence is unsolvable by a fixed alias table
goodhartRisks: filtering out stretch roles to raise apparent precision, which stretchRolesRetainedAtK exposes
contracts.allowedInterpretation: structured requirement-matching correctness
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: hireability, or a prediction of being hired
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Regulated credential equivalence has a legal answer no model should invent.
contracts.currentLimitation: Requirements are structured, so this measures matching rather than requirement extraction (see row 4). Legacy Hireability logic is NOT a substitute for this row.

contracts.productQuestion: Do jobs containing work the person wants to do next rank appropriately, without requiring prior experience?
contracts.construct: Graded ranking quality against planted desired-work coverage.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted direction grade 0-3
mandatoryGuardrails: Experience must not leak into Direction: planted desired atoms are never performed atoms
knownFailureModes: 0.769 NDCG at hard difficulty with 3 of 12 people below the catastrophe threshold, driven by 0.542 mapping abstention on aspiration language
goodhartRisks: inferring direction from experience, which the planted disjointness prevents by construction
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative direction-ranking quality on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: prediction of what the person will actually do next
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Stated direction may differ from revealed direction.
contracts.currentLimitation: Aspiration language is the sparsest and hardest-to-map evidence stream.

contracts.productQuestion: Can TaskDNA find jobs that are BOTH supported by transferable background AND aligned with independent work interests?
contracts.construct: Intersection of two independently planted labels; never a blended score.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked job list from recommendation Mode B
contracts.groundTruth: Planted experience grade >= 2 AND planted preference grade >= 2
mandatoryGuardrails: Experience NDCG@K and Preference NDCG@K must both be reported
knownFailureModes: a joint metric can hide damage to one channel, which is why both single-channel NDCGs are mandatory companions
goodhartRisks: inventing an Overall score, which the mode contract and a test forbid
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative joint-discovery quality on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: a single measure of recommendation quality
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Human judgement of whether a job is both familiar and enjoyable is required.
contracts.currentLimitation: Pareto ordering with a maximin tie-break is a declared policy, not a validated one.

contracts.productQuestion: Can TaskDNA find jobs where experience is moderate but preference and direction are high?
contracts.construct: Planted low-experience, high-direction, positive-preference targets.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked job list from recommendation Mode C
contracts.groundTruth: Planted experience grade <= 1 AND direction grade >= 2 AND preference grade >= 1
mandatoryGuardrails: Mode C must not correlate with Experience Fit
Experience scores must be identical across modes
contracts.naiveBaseline: experience-ordered ranking, which should perform badly here by construction
knownFailureModes: depends on aspiration mapping, currently the weakest stream
goodhartRisks: becoming a resume-replication ranker, which the low-experience requirement prevents
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative transition-discovery quality on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: prediction of transition success
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Whether a transition is achievable is a human and market judgement.
contracts.currentLimitation: Transition targets are planted as fully novel work; partial-overlap transitions are not yet modelled.

contracts.productQuestion: Does TaskDNA surface genuinely relevant jobs that conventional title and resume similarity miss?
contracts.construct: Planted experience relevance reachable only across a title or industry boundary. Surprise WITHOUT relevance is excluded by definition.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted experience grade >= 2 AND (crossTitle OR crossIndustry)
mandatoryGuardrails: lift over title-only and occupation-stratum baselines
knownFailureModes: rewarding random novelty, which is why relevance is a precondition of the label
goodhartRisks: injecting unrelated jobs to raise a novelty number, which noveltyWithoutRelevanceRate exposes
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative cross-boundary discovery on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: human-judged surprise or delight
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Whether a surprising match is welcome is a human judgement.
contracts.currentLimitation: Cross-boundary is operationalized as stratum and industry difference, which is coarser than real occupational distance.

contracts.productQuestion: Given four independent channels, which jobs should be shown, in what order, for a stated product question?
contracts.construct: Four explicit modes with weight-free selection rules.
contracts.predictionOutput: ranked job list plus a per-job reason
contracts.groundTruth: Planted labels for the channels each mode claims to serve
contracts.primaryMetric: per-mode NDCG on the mode's graded channels
mandatoryGuardrails: no Overall score anywhere in a mode result
knownFailureModes: Pareto plus maximin is a declared policy choice, not a validated one
goodhartRisks: quietly introducing blended weights, which a test forbids
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative policy behaviour on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: the best policy for real users
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Which mode a user wants is a product and user-research question.
contracts.currentLimitation: Mode selection is not personalized; the user chooses the question.

contracts.productQuestion: Are declared hard user constraints (location, remote mode, compensation, authorization) never violated?
contracts.construct: Hard-constraint violation rate and soft-constraint satisfaction.
contracts.groundTruth: Declared user constraints
mandatoryGuardrails: constraint filtering must not rewrite any fit channel value
knownFailureModes: NO USER CONSTRAINT FIELDS EXIST in the data model.
goodhartRisks: not applicable while unimplemented
contracts.allowedInterpretation: none
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: any claim that constraints are enforced or measured
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Constraints are user-declared facts, not inferences.
contracts.currentLimitation: No location, remote-mode, compensation, employment-type, schedule, travel, or authorization fields exist on the person or job model. Fabricating them to satisfy a metric would be worse than recording the gap. The trace records the absence explicitly.
contracts.exclusion: EXCLUDED FROM THE 8-HOUR LOOP. Zero constraints are declared, so zero can be violated; this is vacuous rather than passing.

contracts.productQuestion: Does task-based matching find relevant opportunities that conventional title and resume matching miss?
contracts.construct: Absolute lift of TaskDNA over simple reference baselines on the same planted labels.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted labels
contracts.aggregation: TaskDNA value minus best baseline value
contracts.scale: same units as the compared metric
mandatoryGuardrails: report the best baseline and its identity, never only the lift
compare on experience NDCG, cross-title recall, cross-industry recall, and surprising-transfer recall
knownFailureModes: the baselines are deliberately simple and are not strong competitors
resume-lexical is a strong baseline on this corpus and lift over it is small at hard difficulty
goodhartRisks: weakening the baseline instead of improving TaskDNA, which the fixed baseline implementations prevent
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative advantage over simple conventional matching on planted truth
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: advantage over production recommender systems
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: A real comparison needs human relevance labels on real jobs.
contracts.currentLimitation: No embedding baseline: adding one would require infrastructure this preflight deliberately did not build.

contracts.productQuestion: Do recommendation explanations cite only evidence the system actually used?
contracts.construct: Structural grounding of every explanation sentence in a traced channel contribution.
contracts.predictionOutput: explanation sentences plus cited evidence and responsibility ids
contracts.groundTruth: The set of contributions the scoring actually used
mandatoryGuardrails: every cited evidence id must appear in a traced contribution
every cited responsibility id must appear in a traced contribution
channel attribution must match the channel that produced the contribution
knownFailureModes: structural grounding does not establish that a grounded explanation is USEFUL or well-worded
goodhartRisks: emitting only trivially-supported sentences to keep the unsupported rate at zero
contracts.allowedInterpretation: explanations are grounded in used evidence
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: explanation quality, persuasiveness, or human comprehensibility
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Whether an explanation helps a person decide requires human evaluation.
contracts.currentLimitation: Explanations are template sentences over traced contributions. No LLM writes prose yet; when one does, it may only summarize this provenance.

contracts.productQuestion: Does the top-K avoid semantic duplicates while staying relevant?
contracts.construct: Duplicate and near-duplicate rates and facet diversity over the returned set, reported with relevance.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted core-atom sets and facets
mandatoryGuardrails: relevantShare must be reported alongside every diversity number
knownFailureModes: diversity is trivially improved by inserting irrelevant jobs
goodhartRisks: optimizing diversity alone, which is why relevantShare is mandatory
contracts.allowedInterpretation: structural redundancy of the returned set
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: perceived usefulness of the set
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Useful breadth is a human judgement.
contracts.currentLimitation: Near-duplicate detection uses planted atom overlap, which is stronger information than a production system would have.

contracts.productQuestion: Do gains generalize beyond the exact wording the synthetic generator produces?
contracts.construct: Development-to-validation gap across WITHHELD paraphrase families.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted labels on both splits
contracts.scale: same units as the compared metric
mandatoryGuardrails: VALIDATION uses paraphrase families never seen in DEVELOPMENT
difficulty-tier drop (verbatim to standard to hard) isolates surface-wording dependence
repeated DEVELOPMENT gains with VALIDATION degradation are never KEEP
knownFailureModes: only four paraphrase families exist, so family withholding is a coarse generalization test
goodhartRisks: tuning against VALIDATION, which the preregistration protocol forbids
contracts.allowedInterpretation: whether a change survives unseen phrasings
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: generalization to real human language
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Real generalization needs real text.
contracts.currentLimitation: Unseen occupations and unseen occupation families are not yet withheld; only paraphrase families are.

contracts.productQuestion: Does matching one peripheral duty wrongly imply strong relevance?
contracts.construct: Rank comparison between a job matching several central duties and one matching a single peripheral duty.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted core and incidental responsibility sets, weighted by INCIDENTAL_LABEL_WEIGHT
contracts.aggregation: mean rank comparison and over-reward rate
mandatoryGuardrails: O*NET importance metadata is preserved on every atom but is NOT used as an invented weight
knownFailureModes: INCIDENTAL_LABEL_WEIGHT of 0.25 is a declared label-design choice, not an empirically derived weight
goodhartRisks: adjusting the incidental weight to move a metric, which is a metric-contract change
contracts.allowedInterpretation: whether peripheral matches are correctly discounted
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: the correct importance weighting for real jobs
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Which duties are central is a judgement about the specific role.
contracts.currentLimitation: The scoring path does not yet distinguish core from incidental responsibilities; only the LABEL does. That asymmetry is deliberate: it lets the benchmark detect the pathology before any weighting is introduced.

contracts.productQuestion: Does any metric improvement depend on information unavailable at real inference time?
contracts.construct: Invariance under paraphrase, ordering, duplication, title removal, title swap, industry swap, and keyword stuffing; plus absence of hidden-truth and generator-metadata leakage.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted labels and the declared input surface
mandatoryGuardrails: no atom id, planted label, or corpus metadata may appear in pipeline input
knownFailureModes: paraphrase invariance is only tested across the four implemented families
goodhartRisks: reading planted metadata, which an explicit leakage test forbids
contracts.allowedInterpretation: the pipeline sees only what real inference would see
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: robustness to real-world text variation
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Real robustness needs real text.
contracts.currentLimitation: OOD behaviour is covered by the adversarial lab cohort rather than by the planted job corpus.

contracts.productQuestion: Do the numbers the product shows support the interpretation a user would place on them?
contracts.construct: Ranking discrimination, score distribution and saturation, and the confidence-to-error relationship.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted labels
mandatoryGuardrails: mode ordering must be driven by ranking not by score prettiness
knownFailureModes: channel scores are NOT probabilities and must never be shown as percentage likelihoods
diagnosticConfidence is a similarity readout, not a calibrated probability
goodhartRisks: optimizing score cosmetics instead of ranking behaviour
contracts.allowedInterpretation: relative ordering and discrimination
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: any probabilistic reading such as '87% fit'
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Calibration against outcomes requires outcome data.
contracts.currentLimitation: No probabilistic calibration is computed, because no channel score claims to be a probability.

contracts.productQuestion: Does selective contextual reranking beat the cheap deterministic mapper where it is ambiguous?
contracts.construct: Comparison of a reranked candidate set against the deterministic baseline on the same planted targets.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted atom's Task id
contracts.aggregation: accuracy delta over the deterministic baseline
mandatoryGuardrails: deterministic fallback must be recorded and used on abstention
cache key must include model and prompt version
contracts.naiveBaseline: the deterministic lexical mapper, which is the current implementation
knownFailureModes: NO RERANKER IS IMPLEMENTED. The CandidateReranker seam and the LearnedComponent contract exist; nothing is wired.
goodhartRisks: invoking a model on everything
which the invocation-rate cap bounds
contracts.allowedInterpretation: none until a reranker exists
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: any claim that contextual reranking is evaluated
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: Same as rows 5 to 7.
contracts.currentLimitation: The evaluation harness (row 5 to 7 mapping benchmark) accepts a reranker via mapWork's CandidateReranker parameter, so a reranker experiment is runnable the moment one is implemented. The metric has no value yet because there is nothing to measure.
contracts.exclusion: IN SCOPE TO BUILD, not yet measurable. The loop may implement a reranker and then measure it with the existing harness; it may not claim a reranking result before implementing one.

contracts.productQuestion: Can a behaviour change ever be served a stale cached result?
contracts.construct: Cache-key completeness over every behaviour-changing input, plus hit rate and recomputation count.
contracts.groundTruth: Declared behaviour-changing input set
mandatoryGuardrails: context and reranker version must separate entries
MAPPER_CONFIG contents pinned by a test
cache hit returns a bit-identical object
knownFailureModes: a future model-assisted component must add model and prompt version to the key or it will serve stale interpretations
goodhartRisks: caching across a behaviour change to gain speed
contracts.allowedInterpretation: cache correctness and efficiency
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: not applicable
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: not applicable
contracts.currentLimitation: Only the mapper cache exists today.

contracts.productQuestion: Can a developer trace a bad recommendation to the exact subsystem and evidence that caused it, without guessing?
contracts.construct: A structured trace covering every transformation from raw evidence to final rank, with a per-stage verdict.
contracts.groundTruth: Planted truth per stage
mandatoryGuardrails: candidate set and selection reason retained
channel score decomposed to evidence and responsibility
mapper version, corpus hash, and cache key recorded
knownFailureModes: stage verdict thresholds are declared, not derived
goodhartRisks: not applicable
contracts.allowedInterpretation: a failure can be localized to a subsystem
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: not applicable
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: not applicable
contracts.currentLimitation: The trace covers the V3 four-channel path. The legacy 17-dimension path is not traced to the same depth.

contracts.productQuestion: Is the evaluation fast enough to sustain many meaningful experiments?
contracts.construct: Stage-level and end-to-end runtime, plus cache hit rate.
contracts.groundTruth: not applicable
mandatoryGuardrails: corpus build, pipeline, and metric phases reported separately
FAST tier must stay in seconds
contracts.naiveBaseline: pre-cache mapWork at 214 ms per call
knownFailureModes: the product benchmark is the slowest evaluator and belongs in CHECKPOINT, not FAST
goodhartRisks: trading correctness for speed via unsafe caching
contracts.allowedInterpretation: evaluation cost
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: production serving latency
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: not applicable
contracts.currentLimitation: Runtime is measured on this VM only.

contracts.productQuestion: Are TaskDNA's recommendations actually good for real people?
contracts.construct: Human-judged relevance and usefulness of person-job recommendations.
contracts.groundTruth: Independent human annotation or behavioural outcomes
contracts.aggregation: human-labelled NDCG@K, Recall@K, Precision@K, pairwise preference accuracy
mandatoryGuardrails: annotation must be independent of the algorithm
behavioural outcomes carry user-selection and market bias and must not be substituted for construct-valid labels
knownFailureModes: substituting synthetic results for human validity
goodhartRisks: optimizing saves and clicks instead of career usefulness
contracts.allowedInterpretation: none available
contracts.forbiddenInterpretation: NO CURRENT BENCHMARK IN THIS FILE ESTABLISHES THIS. Every other row is autonomous engineering signal only.
contracts.humanValidationBoundary: This row IS the boundary.
contracts.currentLimitation: No human annotation exists. Schemas for future annotation are described in docs/METRIC_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md.
contracts.exclusion: PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED FROM AUTONOMOUS OPTIMIZATION. The loop must never claim human recommendation validity.
